open_questions: Length: built to the R-3896-1 envelope drawing (224.5 in, 5.70 m). The fact sheet says 19 ft (5.79 m), R-3896-1's text 19.2 ft, NASA's 2013 slides 18.4 ft.

Bell contour: no contour published. Built as a 30 to 15 degree bell from the throat (62.5 in below the gimbal) to the 10:1 plane; the manual puts the 3:1 plane "approximately 30 inches below the throat", where this bell is 1.68 m across against 1.53 m for 3:1. A bell that matches both would need a longer nozzle than the envelope allows.
Chamber and oxidizer dome diameters, and the gimbal block, are estimated: R-3896-1 gives no figures. The injector drawings in the R-3896-1A supplement may.
Pipe routing and the turbopump's position are estimated from the drawings and photos.
Finish: bare metal, as in the shop and museum photos; flight engines were wrapped in insulation (fact sheet).
Photo caption 6862832 says 12.5 ft at the exit: that matches R-3896-1's 147 in envelope over the rings (12.25 ft), not the 139 in lip.
No reference model: NASA 3D Resources has only a low-detail Saturn V with plain bells, and the Sketchfab F-1 (Defonten) can't be downloaded and has an editorial licence.

Turbine exhaust manifold: R-3896-1 Figure 2-22 gives 125 in between the torus's centres with a 13.5 in tube at the inlet, which would put its inside edge at 49 in radius, inside the 55 in nozzle at the 10:1 plane. Built hugging the nozzle instead (photo_6862832), so the inlet side reaches about 83 in out, past the drawing's 73.5 in envelope.

source: r3896_1, p.1-8: tubes "identified on reinforcing bands and straps below the thrust chamber throat"; p.1-25 (par. 1-108): "Protruding studs are percussion-welded onto hatbands of the thrust chamber to support and secure insulator panels".
photo_6862832: about twenty bands from the exit to the throat region. Estimated.

karp_illustration: below the ribbed top the bands come in two layers. Bottom (in the illustration y 300-400 at 97.5 px/m: from the exhaust manifold up to about 0.94 m above the 10:1 plane, 42% of the nozzle's length): darker bluish bands set closer together, hardly any straps. Middle (y 125-300: up to about 1.8 m, 80%, where the ribs start): lighter bands with many short straps between neighbouring bands, two to four per gap. Each band is a pair of thin rings with the tube wall showing in the gap between them (the rows of light dashes are the tubes' crowns). Strap angles are placed at random (seeded) to match that look; band counts, sizes, gap and colours (spec materials cres and bright_steel) estimated.
r3896_1, p.1-8: "reinforcing bands and straps below the thrust chamber throat".

tubes.source: r3896_1, p.1-8: "One hundred seventy-eight primary tubes ... make up the chamber body above the 3:1 expansion ratio plane (approximately 30 inches below the throat centerline plane). Three hundred fifty-six one-inch-outside-diameter secondary tubes ... form the chamber from the 3:1 to the 10:1 expansion ratio plane."

source: karp_illustration: the bell's outline, traced at 97.5 px/m (the 1.2 m chamber) from y 366 (its top, which lands on the throat plane) to y 540 (0.44 m above the 10:1 plane, where it matches our outline): it leaves the chamber at about the chamber's width with a rounded shoulder and is up to 0.2 m wider than the nozzle wall in the upper half.
